lessons.title: Growing broilers from placement to slaughter
lessons.html:
Growing broilers from placement to slaughter

Broilers are chickens bred for meat. They grow very fast and are usually sent to the abattoir after a few weeks. Because they grow so quickly, small mistakes in feed, water, heat or air quickly cost weight and money.

The growing cycle

  1. House preparation: clean, disinfect, dry litter, warm the house.
  2. Placement and brooding: day-old chicks are placed and kept warm.
  3. Growing: birds move from starter to grower to finisher feed as the feed company and supervisor plan.
  4. Catching and loading: birds are caught and sent to the abattoir at target weight.
  5. Clean-out: the house is emptied and cleaned for the next flock.

Daily care

  • Water must be available all the time. Check nipple lines and drinkers on every round.
  • Keep feeders filled and set at the right height for the birds' size.
  • Walk through the house slowly so birds get up, move and eat.
  • Remove dead birds and record them every day.
  • Keep litter dry. Wet litter causes burns on feet and breasts and lowers meat quality.

Climate in the house

As broilers grow they make a lot of heat. Big birds suffer in hot weather. Watch for panting and birds lying with wings spread. Use fans, curtains and cooling as your supervisor instructs. In cold weather keep birds warm but still give fresh air, because ammonia from the litter damages eyes and lungs.

Space

Do not crowd birds. Too many birds per square metre causes heat stress, poor growth and disease. Your farm sets the stocking density.

lessons.title: Weighing, records and sending birds to slaughter
lessons.html:
Weighing, records and sending birds to slaughter

Weighing birds

Birds are weighed regularly, often once a week, to see if they are growing to target.

  1. Catch a sample of birds from different parts of the house, not only the biggest or smallest.
  2. Weigh each bird gently on the scale and write down the weight.
  3. Your supervisor works out the average and compares it with the target.

Records

RecordWhy
Daily deaths and cullsEarly warning of disease
Feed delivered and usedWorks out feed conversion: how much feed makes 1 kg of bird
Water usedA drop warns of trouble
WeightsShows if growth is on target
Vaccines and medicinesWithdrawal periods before slaughter

Feed is the biggest cost in broiler production. Wasted feed and slow growth reduce profit.

Before slaughter

  • Check records that any medicine withdrawal period, as on the label, is finished before birds leave.
  • Feed is usually removed some hours before catching, as the abattoir and supervisor instruct, but water stays available until catching.
  • Lift feeder and drinker lines just before catching so birds and people do not trip.

Catching humanely

The Animals Protection Act 71 of 1962 makes cruelty to animals an offence.

  • Catch in dim light to keep birds calm.
  • Hold birds gently by both legs or around the body, as you are trained. Never throw birds or carry them by the neck or one wing.
  • Do not overfill crates.
  • Keep loaded crates in shade and moving air.

Key points

  • Broilers grow fast, so daily care of water, feed and climate is vital.
  • Keep litter dry and do not overcrowd.
  • Weigh a fair sample and keep accurate records.
  • Medicine withdrawal periods must be finished before slaughter.
  • Catch and load birds gently and humanely.
